title: Follow the Plan, Then Grade the Trade
hook: Your P&L grades the outcome. Your journal grades the trader.

launchpad.outcome: Grade management quality separately from the outcome, starting with the plan, not the money.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Did I manage it according to my plan?

slides.title: Grade the management

items.text: Trade A: correct entry, correct management, target hit.
Trade B: correct entry, correct management, stop hit.
items.miss: The management was right. The outcome was a loss.

items.text: Trade C: correct entry, panics, takes +10. The original target hits later.
items.miss: It made money. It still broke the plan.

items.text: Trade D: removes the stop, price reverses, large loss.

slides.punch: BAD PROCESS + WIN IS STILL DANGEROUS REINFORCEMENT.

items.text: Did I manage the trade according to my plan?

slides.heading: Planned, actual, outcome: stored apart

beats.title: Planned
beats.line: Entry, stop, target, contracts, model, partial / runner / BE rules, early intervention.

beats.title: Actual
beats.line: Stop changes, target changes, partials, size changes, manual exit, violations, adherence.

beats.title: Outcome
beats.line: Result, realized R, realized P&L, reflection.

slides.punch: A GOOD TRADE IS NEVER CALCULATED FROM PROFIT > 0.

slides.quote: Your P&L grades the outcome. Your journal grades the trader.

slides.prompt: What’s the difference between outcome and management quality?
slides.modelAnswer: The outcome is what the market gave me. Management quality is whether I followed the plan I locked. A trade can lose with perfect management, or win with a violation.

takeaways: Ask “did I follow the plan?” first.
remember: Your P&L grades the outcome. Your journal grades the trader.
